Hi Tariq — thanks for the clear list. I put together a short comparison and attached a one-pager plus a draft proposal grid. High level first:

- Invoicing / billing:
  * AWS/Azure Marketplace (SaaS) billing is handled by the marketplace provider (AWS/Azure) in most cases — you receive a single consolidated invoice from AWS/Azure reflecting marketplace charges; line items indicate the SaaS vendor. Usage reporting is available through the marketplace, but some customers prefer Redwood-issued invoices for internal chargeback or tax reasons.
  * Direct MSA with Redwood: Redwood issues monthly invoices directly to your AP with our standard invoicing terms and GL-friendly line items. We can provide detailed usage exports for your billing system.

- Commercial terms & SLAs:
  * Marketplace: the marketplace listing typically layers a marketplace terms wrapper over our offering; certain negotiated terms (e.g., liability caps, indemnities) can be limited by marketplace policies. For material legal or security changes we usually recommend a direct MSA.
  * Direct: full MSA negotiation gives you the most control (custom SLAs, audit rights, data residency addenda).

- Co-sell / credits:
  * AWS co-sell can surface your procurement to AWS account teams and may unlock deal credits / funding depending on partner status and co-sell registration. However, co-sell benefits often require registration and AWS approval cycles (and sometimes minimum contract work).
  * Azure/GCP offer similar partner incentives but the onboarding differs (Azure Marketplace co-sell requires specific ISV registration and listing configuration).

- Timeline & customizability:
  * Marketplace route can accelerate procurement for teams that mandate marketplace purchases (no legal redlines). But marketplace listings are less flexible for bespoke commercial terms or custom data handling commitments.
  * Direct MSA takes longer but supports custom OKRs: custom reporting, audit SLA, and bespoke integration work.

Tariq — adding the implementation + co-sell mechanics at a glance:

- AWS Marketplace (SaaS) path:
  1) Redwood submits listing and pricing (metered usage SKU) — marketplace takes care of meter billing.
  2) To get co-sell incentives, we must register the opportunity in AWS PRC and get AWS account team to co-sell — this typically requires an MDR (marketing development request) and can take 1–3 weeks of coordination.
  3) Invoices: AWS invoices NorthStar; Redwood receives payout on marketplace cadence.
  4) Entitlements: AWS entitlements model supports seat or usage IDs; we can provide usage export to match PO.

- Direct MSA path:
  1) Redwood issues a quote and MSA/SOW; payment goes to Redwood AP.
  2) For enterprise customers we offer invoice frequency (monthly/quarterly), custom PO fields, and GL mappings.
  3) If you want AWS incentives but prefer a direct MSA, we can set up a pass-through co-sell or reseller flow but that complicates invoicing and credit recognition.

Tradeoffs to call out for your legal team:
- Marketplace restricts certain negotiated terms (IP carve-outs, some indemnities).
- Marketplace often makes it harder to do custom DPA or on-prem addenda — direct MSA better for strict residency/audit requirements.

I'll loop in our partner contact from CloudBridge who can outline reseller + marketplace combinations and timing.

Tariq — quick summary and recommended next steps so your team can circulate:

Summary:
- Marketplace (AWS/Azure): faster procurement for teams that require marketplace purchases; consolidated vendor invoice from the cloud provider; easier for standard/untailored deployments; co-sell can add incentives but requires registration and coordination with AWS/Azure account teams.
- Direct MSA: slower but gives you full control over negotiated terms (SLA customizations, DPA, audit rights) and direct invoicing/reporting. Better for regulated workloads or bespoke deployment guarantees.
- Hybrid: use a reseller/partner (CloudBridge) to get consolidated billing + co-sell path while preserving some contractual flexibilities.

Recommended next steps:
1) If NorthStar's internal procurement is marketplace-first for small pilots, proceed with Marketplace listing and we will enable entitlements so you can start a pilot within 1–2 weeks.
